standard_prerequisites.use: Produces, for each point of the fibre, elementary etale neighbourhoods of the base and of the source whose global sections of the pulled back module are projective over the ring of the base neighbourhood; assembling finitely many of them is what the counted proof supplies.

standard_prerequisites.name: Projectivity ascends along a base change of rings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-ascend-properties-modules, invoked at proof line 3400
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the direct sum of the base changes of the pointwise projective modules is again projective over the ring of the new base.

core_obligations: Cover the fibre pointwise: for each point x of the fibre apply the pointwise proposition to obtain elementary etale neighbourhoods and an affine etale neighbourhood Y_x of x whose global sections of the pulled back module are projective over the ring of the base neighbourhood, and note that its image meets the fibre in an open neighbourhood of x (proof lines 3366-3380).

Pass to finitely many points and dominate: since the fibre is quasi-compact, finitely many of those neighbourhoods cover it, and one chooses an elementary etale neighbourhood of the base dominating all of them, which may also be taken affine (proof lines 3381-3388).

Assemble and conclude projectivity: take the disjoint union of the base changed pieces as the new source with the obvious etale morphism, whose image contains the fibre, and compute the global sections of the pulled back module as a direct sum of base changes of projective modules, which is projective over the ring of the new affine base (proof lines 3389-3400).
proof_roadmap: Cover the fibre by the pointwise projective pieces (proof lines 3366-3380).
Choose one dominating elementary etale neighbourhood, affine (proof lines 3381-3388).
Take the disjoint union of the base changed pieces and use ascent of projectivity (proof lines 3389-3400).
difficulty_reason: The lemma globalises the pointwise statement: for a finite presentation morphism and a finitely presented module flat at every point of a fibre, there is an elementary etale neighbourhood of the point of the base and an affine etale neighbourhood of the fibre on which the pulled back module has projective global sections (statement lines 3341-3364, tag 05KW). The proof applies the pointwise proposition at each point of the quasi-compact fibre, passes to finitely many points, chooses one dominating elementary etale neighbourhood, and then takes the disjoint union of the base changed pieces, whose global sections are a direct sum of base changes of projective modules and hence projective by ascent. The assembling step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
